## 8Z.35 Phase 34: S3-compatible storage, server-side image compression, promotion image upload, vendor PAN document (KYC) (2026-10-09)

`packages/shared-types`, `packages/db`, `apps/api`, `apps/admin`, `apps/mobile`. Migration
**0036**. New dependencies: `@aws-sdk/client-s3` and `sharp` (API), `expo-image-manipulator`
(mobile, native: **the development client must be rebuilt**; the camera permission string in
`app.json` is new too). SPEC.md was not changed. **Not run against a real bucket, a browser or a
device**; the dev database needs `pnpm db:migrate`.

### Asked vs built (documented contracts and SPEC kept)

| Asked                                                  | Built                                                                                                                                                                    | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pan_document_url` "to securely store the location"    | the column, holding the **object key** of the document in a **private** bucket (`kyc/pan/<vendor>/<uuid>.webp`); no response ever carries it                             | A PAN certificate is an identity document. A URL on the public CDN would be readable by anyone who obtained it, for good. The bytes are reachable only through the API, behind the Super Admin's token |
| (not asked) a way to see the document                  | `GET /api/admin/vendors/:id/pan-document` (streams the image), `has_pan_document` on the compliance list, a "View document" dialog on the Compliance tab                 | Without it the upload verifies nothing: §8Z.19 recorded "a Super Admin has nothing to open when verifying"                                                                                             |
| (not asked) reading what is on file                    | `GET /api/vendor/tax-identity`                                                                                                                                           | The Vendor App has to know whether a document is on file and whether it is verified (it warns before replacing a verified one)                                                                         |
| "stream uploads directly to the cloud bucket"          | one `PutObject` per image with the bytes as its body, from memory. No temporary file, no multipart upload                                                                | The compression rule needs the whole image in memory to re-encode it and to measure the result; what is then sent is under 300 KB                                                                      |
| one bucket                                             | **two**: `S3_PUBLIC_BUCKET` (behind `S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`) and `S3_PRIVATE_BUCKET`; the env refuses the same name for both                                                | Public/private is a bucket setting on R2, not a per-object one                                                                                                                                         |
| replace local disk storage                             | `STORAGE_DRIVER=LOCAL \| S3`. LOCAL stays for development and tests and **is refused with `NODE_ENV=production`**                                                        | Local runs and 900 integration tests need no bucket. Production on a container's disk loses every file on redeploy                                                                                     |
| `deleteFile(url)`                                      | on every storage. It deletes **only** a URL that storage issued (its base URL, its area, a generated `<uuid>.<ext>` name); anything else returns false and sends nothing | `image_url` and `image_urls` accept any http(s) URL: a pasted link must never become a delete in our bucket                                                                                            |
| (not asked) cleaning up an upload that was never saved | `DELETE /api/admin/promotions/image { url }` (409 while a promotion uses it); the admin form calls it on Cancel and for replaced tries                                   | An image is uploaded before its promotion is saved; a cancelled form would otherwise leave an object nothing names                                                                                     |
| "compress the image on the client-side"                | `expo-image-manipulator`: longer side to 1200 px, JPEG at 75%. The server re-encodes it once more to WebP                                                                | SPEC infrastructure §6 names `react-native-compressor`; the request named Expo's tool, which needs no extra native module beyond itself. The stored format is the server's in either case              |
| compress "before final storage, as per SPEC"           | applied to **every** image upload: dispute evidence, product photos, promotion art, PAN documents                                                                        | SPEC's rule is not per route. **Behaviour change:** evidence and product photos are now stored as `.webp` (`content_type: image/webp`); files stored earlier keep their names and are still deletable  |

> **Updated by §8Z.36 (2026-10-09):** verification now requires a document (`422 DOCUMENT_MISSING`), a changed PAN number removes the uploaded document, and the Vendor App sends the PAN and the VAT flag. The second and third bullets below, and the first item under "Open", are superseded.

### Decided here, to confirm

- **Replacing the document of a verified PAN clears the verification** (payouts wait for a new
  check; the shop keeps trading). The Super Admin checked the document that is being deleted. A
  first document on an already verified PAN (the seeded shops) clears nothing. The Vendor App asks
  before it replaces a verified document.
- **Verification does not require a document.** `POST …/pan-verification` still needs only a PAN
  on file (the seed verifies shops that have none). Requiring one is a one-line change.
- **A changed PAN number keeps the uploaded document.** The verification is already cleared by
  the PAN change; the admin sees the old document beside the new number.
- **LOCAL is refused in production** (above).

### Migration 0036 (`0036_vendor_kyc_docs.sql`)

`vendors.pan_document_url text NULL` + CHECK `vendors_pan_document_url_check` (null or
non-blank). In `vendorSchema` and `contract.ts`. No backfill.

### Storage (`apps/api/src/uploads/`)

```
routes ── storedImageOf (sniff → sharp) ──▶ EvidenceStorage / ProductImageStorage /
                                            PromotionImageStorage / KycDocumentStorage
                                                   │ PublicFileArea (URL ⇄ key)   │ key only
                                                   ▼                               ▼
                                            ObjectStore: LocalObjectStore | S3ObjectStore
```

| File                         | What                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `object-store.ts`            | `ObjectStore { put, get, delete }`; `LocalObjectStore(rootDir)`; `S3ObjectStore(client, bucket)` (PutObject / GetObject / DeleteObject); `assertObjectKey` refuses any key the storages do not generate |
| `public-files.ts`            | `PublicFileArea(store, publicBaseUrl, area)`: `save` → URL, `keyOf(url, scope?)`, `deleteFile(url, scope?)`; `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (names are random and never reused)   |
| `evidence-storage.ts`        | `ObjectEvidenceStorage` (+ `deleteFile`); `LocalEvidenceStorage` is the same over a directory                                                                                                           |
| `product-image-storage.ts`   | `ObjectProductImageStorage` (`remove(productId, url)` scoped, `deleteFile(url)`); `LocalProductImageStorage`                                                                                            |
| `promotion-image-storage.ts` | `promotions/<uuid>.webp`; `save`, `owns`, `deleteFile`                                                                                                                                                  |
| `kyc-document-storage.ts`    | private store: `savePanDocument` → key, `read(key)`, `deleteFile(key)`; `Cache-Control: private, no-store`                                                                                              |
| `storage-from-env.ts`        | `localFileStorage`, `s3FileStorage(client, { publicBucket, privateBucket, publicBaseUrl })`, `fileStorageFromEnv`                                                                                       |
| `image-compression.ts`       | `compressImage(bytes, limits?)`                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `image-upload.ts`            | `singleImageUpload(field, maxBytes)` (multer: memory, `fileSize`, `files: 1`, `fields: 0`, `parts: 1`), `storedImageOf(bytes, what)`                                                                    |

- **Keys:** `dispute-evidence/<order>/<uuid>.webp`, `product-images/<product>/<uuid>.webp`,
  `promotions/<uuid>.webp` (public bucket); `kyc/pan/<vendor>/<uuid>.webp` (private bucket).
- **LOCAL:** public files under `UPLOADS_DIR` (served at `/uploads` as before); KYC documents
  under `UPLOADS_PRIVATE_DIR` (default `apps/api/uploads-private`, git-ignored), which nothing
  serves. **S3:** the API mounts no static directory; files are read from `S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`.
- **Env** (`serverEnvSchema`, `.env.example`): `STORAGE_DRIVER`, `S3_ENDPOINT` (R2:
  `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`; empty for AWS), `S3_REGION` (default `auto`),
  `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` + `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (both or neither: without them the SDK's own chain,
  e.g. a task role), `S3_PUBLIC_BUCKET`, `S3_PRIVATE_BUCKET`, `S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (https in
  production), `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` (MinIO), `UPLOADS_PRIVATE_DIR`.
- **Bucket setup the code assumes:** the public bucket is readable at `S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (an R2
  custom domain or `r2.dev`); the private bucket has no public access. The API key needs
  PutObject, GetObject and DeleteObject on both. No ACL is ever sent.
- The worker parses the same env and builds no storage.

### Compression (`compressImage`, SPEC infrastructure §6)

1. The type is the file's own signature (`sniffEvidenceType`: JPEG, PNG, WebP), never the declared
   Content-Type or name: else `415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`.
2. sharp must decode it as one of those three (a signature followed by junk, a GIF, an SVG: 415).
   A decoded image over 50 megapixels is refused before it is inflated.
3. Turned upright from its EXIF orientation; **all metadata dropped** (camera, time, GPS).
4. Longer side to 1200 px (`fit: inside`, never enlarged), WebP at quality 75.
5. Still 300 KB or more: quality 65, 55, 45, 35; then the picture is scaled down by a fifth and the
   steps repeat, down to 320 px. Nothing at or over 300 KB is ever stored
   (`422 IMAGE_NOT_COMPRESSIBLE`; not reachable with a real photo).
6. An animated image is stored as its first frame.

Measured: a 6 MB JPEG of random noise (the worst case) → 1200 × 960 WebP, 280 KB, at quality 45.
The upload limit before compression stays 5 MB per image (`413 FILE_TOO_LARGE`).

### Routes

```jsonc
// POST /api/admin/promotions/image        SUPER_ADMIN · multipart, one `image` part (≤ 5 MB)
//   201 { "url": "https://cdn…/promotions/<uuid>.webp" }
//   400 VALIDATION_FAILED (no file) · 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST (another field, a second file, a wrong part name)
//   413 FILE_TOO_LARGE · 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE
// DELETE /api/admin/promotions/image { "url" }   → 204 (also when gone, or not ours) · 409 PROMOTION_IMAGE_IN_USE
// POST /api/vendor/tax-identity/document  VENDOR (own shop, any status) · multipart, one `document` part (≤ 5 MB)
//   201 { "vendor_id", "has_pan_document": true, "replaced": false, "verification_cleared": false, "pan_verified_at": null }
//   the same refusals · 404 VENDOR_NOT_FOUND
// GET  /api/vendor/tax-identity           VENDOR
//   200 { "vendor_id", "tax_id" | null, "is_vat_registered", "legal_name", "registered_address", "status",
//         "pan_verified_at" | null, "has_pan_document" }
// GET  /api/admin/vendors/:id/pan-document   SUPER_ADMIN → 200 image/webp (no-store, nosniff)
//   404 PAN_DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND (none uploaded, or its object is gone) · 404 VENDOR_NOT_FOUND
// GET  /api/admin/compliance/vendors      each vendor gains "has_pan_document" (defaults to false)
```

`/promotions/image` is registered before `/promotions/:id`. Contracts: shared-types
`api/admin-marketing.ts`, `api/vendor-settings.ts`, `api/admin-governance.ts`; constants
`STORED_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION` 1200, `STORED_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES` 300 KB, `PROMOTION_IMAGE_FILE_FIELD`,
`PAN_DOCUMENT_FILE_FIELD`, `MAX_PROMOTION_IMAGE_BYTES`, `MAX_PAN_DOCUMENT_BYTES`. Audit action
`PAN_DOCUMENT_UPLOADED` (on `vendor`; 44 actions).

### S3 lifecycle: what is deleted, when, and what a failure leaves

The bucket and PostgreSQL cannot commit together, so every flow is ordered so that **a row never
names a missing object**. The worst outcome is an object nothing names: it costs storage, is
logged (`{"storage":"orphan_object","kind":…}` on `console.warn`), and is invisible.

**PAN document** (`VendorComplianceService.uploadPanDocument`):

| Step                                                                                                                                 | If it fails                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1. `PutObject` the new document under a new key                                                                                      | 500. Row and old document untouched                                |
| 2. One transaction, vendor row `FOR UPDATE`: `pan_document_url` = new key, verification cleared if it replaced a verified one, audit | 500. **The new object is deleted**; row and old document untouched |
| 3. After the commit: `DeleteObject` the key the row named before                                                                     | 201 all the same. The old object stays as a logged orphan          |

- Two uploads at once queue on the row lock; the second sees the first's key as "previous" and
  deletes it. Five simultaneous uploads leave exactly one object, the one the row names (tested).
- A crash between steps 1 and 2, or 2 and 3, also leaves one orphan. **Nothing sweeps orphans.**

**Promotion artwork** (`PromotionService`):

| Event                                         | Effect on the bucket                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PUT` names another image (or none)           | after the commit, the old image is deleted **if no other promotion names it** and it is one this API issued   |
| `DELETE` a promotion                          | the same, for its image                                                                                       |
| `PUT` with the same image, or a refused write | nothing                                                                                                       |
| the form is cancelled, or a try is replaced   | the admin app calls `DELETE /api/admin/promotions/image`; the server refuses while a promotion uses the image |
| a delete fails                                | the request still succeeds (the row is already changed); logged orphan                                        |

**Product photos** (unchanged logic, now on the bucket): a `PUT` that drops a photo deletes its
object; a refused upload (the 8-photo limit, a race) deletes what it had just stored; one bad
file in a request stores nothing. **Dispute evidence** is never deleted: a transcript keeps its
photos (`deleteFile` exists and is unused).

### Admin app

- **Promotions:** the URL field is a file picker (`accept` JPEG / PNG / WebP; type and 5 MB
  checked before the request). Choosing a file uploads at once: a spinner and "Uploading…", then
  a thumbnail with **Remove image**. Save is disabled while an upload is on its way. The table
  shows each promotion's thumbnail. An image already saved as an external URL is shown and kept
  until removed or replaced; a URL can no longer be typed.
- **Compliance:** "View document" (or "No document uploaded") under each PAN. The dialog fetches
  the image with the admin's token (`ApiClient.download`, same 401 renewal as every call), shows
  it from an object URL and revokes that URL on close.

### Vendor App (`app/(vendor)/settings.tsx` → `features/vendor/PanDocumentCard.tsx`)

- In the Tax identity section: the document's standing (none / awaiting verification / verified
  on a date, from `GET /api/vendor/tax-identity`), **Take a photo** and **Choose from gallery**
  ("Replace from gallery" once one is on file).
- **Permissions** (`pan-document.ts#pickPanDocument`): the camera or photo permission is
  requested only when its button is pressed. Refused → an alert that says what it is for and
  that the shop cannot be verified to go LIVE and be paid without it. If the system will not ask
  again (`canAskAgain: false`), the alert offers **Open Settings** (`Linking.openSettings`). The
  other source stays usable. "Limited" photo access is enough.
- **Compression** (`preparePanDocument`): longer side to 1200 px (never enlarged), JPEG at 75%,
  before the upload. The picker itself runs at quality 1 so there is one lossy step.
- While preparing and uploading: a spinner, both buttons disabled. The photo just sent is shown
  as the preview (the stored document is private and is not fetched back).
- Replacing a **verified** document asks first ("payouts are paused until Hamro Pasal verifies the
  new one"). Failures are worded (too large, not a photo, no connection, camera unavailable) and
  never retried automatically.
- `app.json`: `cameraPermission` was `false`; it is now a sentence, and `photosPermission`
  mentions the PAN document.

### Open

- **The PAN number itself is still saved on the phone only.** The settings form does not call
  `PUT /api/vendor/tax-identity`, so a vendor can upload a document from the app while the server
  holds no PAN for it, and an admin then cannot verify (`409 PAN_MISSING`). Wiring that PUT (it
  needs `is_vat_registered`, which the form has no field for) is the next step for a working
  KYC flow from the app. `GET /api/vendor/tax-identity` now exists to read the current values.
- **Not run against a real bucket.** `S3ObjectStore` is tested through an in-memory stand-in for
  the SDK client (`test/support/fake-s3.ts`); R2's own behaviour (the endpoint, signing, a
  DeleteObject on a missing key) is taken from the S3 API, not observed. Do one upload, read and
  delete against the real buckets before relying on it.
- **Existing files are not migrated.** URLs already in `image_urls` / chat attachments point at
  `…/uploads/…` on the API host. Switching to S3 stops the API serving them: copy
  `apps/api/uploads` into the public bucket and rewrite the stored URLs, or keep the old host up.
- **Orphans are logged, not swept.** A lifecycle rule cannot tell an orphan from a live object; a
  periodic "objects no row names" job would.
- The private document is proxied through the API (≤ 300 KB each). A presigned URL would take
  the bytes off the API; it would also make a shareable link, which is why it was not done.
- The vendor cannot view its stored document, only the photo it just took.
- No rate limit on uploads. An admin can upload promotion images without limit.
- `sharp` ships a native binary per platform: the API image must install dependencies **inside**
  the target image (or with `--os=linux --cpu=x64`), not copy `node_modules` from a Windows host.
- The admin screens and the mobile card were not opened in a browser or on a device. The new
  Nepali strings are unreviewed.

## 8Z.34 Phase 33: discount stacking in checkout, Devanagari in the invoice PDF, Vendor App invoices and offers wired, customer checkout on the real quote (2026-10-09)

`packages/shared-types`, `packages/db`, `packages/ledger`, `apps/api`, `apps/mobile`. Migration
**0035**. New dependencies: `fontkit` (API, already present through pdfkit; now direct),
`expo-file-system` and `expo-sharing` (mobile, both native: **the development client must be
rebuilt**). SPEC.md was not changed. **Not run on a device or against a live API**; the dev
database needs `pnpm db:migrate`.

### Decisions (user, 2026-10-09)

| Topic                 | Decision                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Devanagari in the PDF | Required for IRD compliance. `NotoSansDevanagari-Regular.ttf` (OFL) is a server asset; pdfkit registers it |
| Offer status          | The derived status and `POST /api/vendor/offers/:id/end` stay exactly as built (§8Z.33)                    |
| Scheduled offers      | None. An offer starts when it is created; no `starts_at` in the body                                       |

### Asked vs built

| Asked                                                | Built                                                                                                                                                   | Why                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "use this font for all text"                         | Devanagari runs are drawn with Noto Sans Devanagari; **Latin runs stay in the built-in Helvetica**, on one shared baseline                              | **Noto Sans Devanagari contains no Latin letters** (checked with fontkit: A–Z, a–z and `·` have no glyph). Drawn alone, every English word on the invoice would be empty boxes                    |
| lock order "Vendor Row -> Opt-in Row FOR SHARE"      | vendor row `FOR KEY SHARE` → **vendor offer row `FOR SHARE`** → opt-in row `FOR SHARE` → the inserts                                                    | The offer is re-read under a lock for the same reason the opt-in is. Ending an offer takes vendor row `FOR UPDATE` then the offer row: the same order, so the two cannot deadlock                 |
| store `vendor_offer_id`, `vendor_offer_discount_npr` | as asked. **No copy of the offer rule** is stored (§8Z.5 sketched one in `discount_snapshot`)                                                           | A `vendor_offers` row is immutable (trigger of 0034), so the id is the rule exactly as applied. `discount_snapshot` stays the campaign's                                                          |
| "enforcing its own thresholds" for the campaign      | the campaign's `min_cart_npr` is judged on **what is left after the vendor offer**, like its percentage                                                 | The request's wording ("apply to the remaining subtotal, enforcing its own thresholds"). §8Z.5 can be read as "on the subtotal". **To confirm**; it is one argument in `priceCart`                |
| handle `409 QUOTE_CHANGED` in the app                | also built `expected_total_npr` on `POST /api/cart/checkout` (optional; §8Z.5's contract) and `details.quote` on the 409                                | Without it the 409 fired only in a millisecond race: an offer that ended a minute after the quote was silently charged at the higher price. The amount is compared, never used as a price         |
| "Download PDF … save / display the PDF buffer"       | `fetch` with the session → bytes → `File.write` (expo-file-system) in the cache → `Sharing.shareAsync`                                                  | The share sheet is how a phone views, prints or saves a PDF. `File.downloadFileAsync` was not used: it exposes neither the status nor `X-Invoice-Copy-Number`                                     |
| "eradicate … legacy mock promo logic"                | every mock that touched **money** is gone (list below). The development-only shop extras on cards (rating, cover, `top_offer` label, locality) are kept | They are §8Z.3's Home mocks, used by the feed, shop header and promotion filters and their tests. **A dev build can therefore still show a mock "10% OFF" label on a card that no order honours** |

### 1. Stacking (SPEC core 7 and 9; verification 5)

```
S   = sum(price x quantity)                      database prices
Dv  = best of the shop's running offers on S     FLAT: value; PERCENTAGE: min(S x value%, cap); 0 below its min cart
Dp  = best campaign on (S - Dv)                  same rule, min cart judged on S - Dv; 0 without the shop's ACTIVE opt-in
Dpv = round_half_up(Dp x vendor_share_percent)   Dpp = Dp - Dpv
F   = delivery charge                            never discounted; free-above threshold judged on S
T   = S - Dv - Dp + F
C   = round_half_up(rate x (S - Dv - Dpv))       0 on SUBSCRIPTION
```

- `pricing.ts`: `VendorOfferRule`, `bestVendorOffer` (the larger discount; between equal ones
  the older offer), `priceCart(…, campaigns, vendorOffers)`, `pricedCartView` (the amounts as the
  quote and the 409 carry them). The minimum order value is still judged on S.
- `CheckoutService.runningVendorOffers`: the shop's offers with `ended_at IS NULL`, started, and
  `ends_at` null or in the future, on the database clock. At most 10 rows (the creation limit).
- **Quote:** `vendor_offer: { id: <offer id>, label: <the offer's stored label>, discount_npr }`.
- **Checkout**, inside the order's transaction: the offer row is re-read `FOR SHARE` (`ended_at
IS NULL` and not past `ends_at`, in SQL); ended since the cart was priced → `409 QUOTE_CHANGED`,
  no order, the Redis hold released.
- **`expected_total_npr`** (optional, `>= 0`): compared in paisa with the server's total before
  anything is reserved; different → `409 QUOTE_CHANGED` with
  `details.quote { subtotal_npr, vendor_offer, platform_promo, delivery_fee_npr, total_npr }`.
  The 409 from the in-transaction re-check carries no `details`.
- **Migration 0035:** `orders.vendor_offer_id` → `vendor_offers` (RESTRICT, partial index),
  `orders.vendor_offer_discount_npr` (default 0); CHECK `orders_vendor_offer_check`: discount ≥ 0,
  a discount exactly with its offer, and `vendor offer + campaign discount <= subtotal`. In
  `orderSchema` and `contract.ts`. Existing orders carry 0.
- **`OrderView`** gained `vendor_offer_discount_npr` and `platform_promo_discount_npr` (both
  default 0 in the schema, so an app build reads an older API as "no discount").

**Settlement** (`planSettlement`; `orderTotalPaisa` and the new `orderDiscountPaisa`):

| Order              | Postings                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| prepaid            | escrow −(S−Dv−Dp+F), vendor +(S−Dv−Dpv−C) [+F own delivery], rider [+F], revenue +C, PROMO_EXPENSE −Dpp |
| cash, own delivery | vendor +(Dpp−C), revenue +C, PROMO_EXPENSE −Dpp (unchanged: Dv is the vendor's own)                     |
| cash, fleet        | rider −(S−Dv−Dp+F), vendor +(S−Dv−Dpv−C), revenue +C, rider +F, PROMO_EXPENSE −Dpp                      |

- The vendor funds all of Dv: it comes off what the customer pays and off what the vendor earns,
  and no other account moves for it.
- Read from the same columns: the eSewa `amount` (goods = total − delivery), the Khalti amount
  and both confirmation checks (through `orderTotalPaisa`), pending escrow, the vendor's "cut" in
  the finance ledger, the refund-due amount, and the invoice.
- **Invoice:** `discount_npr` = Dv + Dp; every discount lowers the taxable amount; the grand
  total still must equal the order total or the delivery aborts.

**Verification 5, measured end to end** (`discount-stacking.int.test.ts`): S 1000, FLAT 100,
campaign 10% at 50% vendor share, F 50, rate 10% → Dv 100, Dp 90 (45 / 45), **T 860**,
**C 85.50 on a base of 855**, eSewa signed for `860` (goods `810`), pending escrow 819.50,
wallet +819.50, revenue +85.50, PROMO_EXPENSE −45, escrow back to its start, invoice discount
190 and grand total 860.

### 2. Devanagari in the invoice PDF

- **Assets:** `apps/api/assets/fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Regular.ttf` (required),
  `NotoSansDevanagari-Bold.ttf` (optional; headings fall back to the regular weight), `OFL.txt`,
  `README.md`. **The two font files and the licence were downloaded from the Noto project during
  this work so the tests could run; they are untracked. Commit them or replace them with your own
  copy.** A container image must copy `apps/api/assets` beside `dist`.
- `invoices/invoice-fonts.ts`: `loadInvoiceFonts(dir)` (null without the regular file; reads
  metrics and coverage with fontkit), `splitByScript(text, face)`, `InvoiceFontUnavailableError`.
- `invoice-pdf.ts`: `renderInvoicePdf(row, copy, { fonts })`. A small layout engine (`mixedText`)
  replaces pdfkit's own wrapping:
  - text is cut into runs per script; Latin-1 goes to Helvetica, anything else the Devanagari
    face covers goes to it, and a character neither covers is `?` (never dropped);
  - words wrap at spaces; a word wider than its column is cut between grapheme clusters
    (`Intl.Segmenter`), never inside a conjunct; a space is drawn in the font of the word before
    it, so a Nepali phrase is one run;
  - every run of a line is drawn on one baseline, and a line holding Devanagari is taller;
  - shaping (conjuncts, reph, matra reordering) is fontkit's, through pdfkit.
- **With the font:** the IRD's Nepali field names are printed beside the English ones
  (`Bill No. / बिजक नम्बर`, `Fiscal Year / आर्थिक वर्ष`, `Date (BS) / मिति`; SPEC Nepal section 5).
- **Without it:** a non-production API prints Latin only (as before) and warns at startup;
  **production refuses to print** (`503 INVOICE_PRINT_UNAVAILABLE`, before any copy number is
  taken). Decided here, not asked: an invoice whose names print as `?` is not an IRD document.
- Deterministic as before: the same row, copy number and fonts give the same bytes.
- **Not seen.** No PDF rasteriser is installed on this machine, so no rendered page was looked
  at. Verified instead: glyph-level shaping of the installed font, and which font every string
  is drawn with. **Print one invoice and read it before relying on it** (line heights, the
  bilingual labels' column width, Devanagari in the bold heading).
- Devanagari numerals for amounts (SPEC Nepal section 5, "under the `ne` locale") are not
  printed: the invoice has no locale.

`packages/shared-types`, `packages/db`, `packages/ledger`, `apps/api`. Migrations **0033** and

lays out the invoice from JSON could alter it before printing. This replaces the JSON

### 1. Retroactive invoices (`VendorComplianceService.saveTaxIdentity`)

- **When.** The save that gives the shop its first PAN. In that transaction, after the vendor
  row is updated (so the invoices copy the PAN, VAT registration, legal name and address this
  save leaves), every DELIVERED order of the shop with no invoice gets one, oldest
  `delivered_at` first. Bill Numbers therefore follow the deliveries; the invoices are dated and
  numbered **now** (no invoice could exist before the seller had a PAN, §8Z.11).
- **Response:** `taxIdentityResponseSchema` gained `waiting_invoices_issued` (defaults to 0, so a
  client reads an older API as "none"). Audit: one `WAITING_INVOICES_ISSUED` entry (new action,
  on `vendor`) with `issued_count`, `first_invoice_sequence`, `last_invoice_sequence` and
  `refused_order_ids`; none when no order waited.
- **An order that cannot be invoiced** (`InvoiceNotIssuableError`: its lines do not add up to
  what the customer paid) is skipped and named in `refused_order_ids`. It takes no number (the
  generator refuses before the counter moves) and does not keep the shop from saving its PAN.
  **Nothing retries it.**
- **Lock order** (one order for every path that issues an invoice):

  | Path                             | Order rows                                                 | Vendor row                                                   | Sequence row       |
  | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
  | delivery, nightly reconciliation | its order `FOR UPDATE` (first)                             | `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (wallet journal), then `FOR SHARE` (new) | `FOR UPDATE`, last |
  | PAN save                         | the waiting orders `FOR UPDATE`, in delivery order (first) | `FOR UPDATE`                                                 | `FOR UPDATE`, last |
  - The PAN save reads the shop (id, "has a PAN") unlocked first; both facts are stable (an
    account's shop never changes, a PAN is never removed). Only a shop without a PAN locks orders.
  - Under the vendor lock it re-selects the waiting orders `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`: it holds
    the ones from the first pass, picks up any delivered since, and **never waits for an order
    row while holding the vendor row**. An order skipped there is held by a delivery or the
    reconciliation, which then reads the vendor row after this commit and issues the invoice
    itself.
  - **`generateFiscalInvoice` now reads the seller `FOR SHARE`.** Without it a delivery that
    posts no wallet journal (a 0 % cash order of the shop's own delivery) could read "no PAN"
    while the save, not yet seeing that delivery, skipped it: an order with no invoice from
    either side. With it one of the two always sees the other (tested with a held transaction).
    `FOR SHARE` is never stronger than what a wallet journal already holds, so §8Z.30's rule
    stands.

- **Known gap:** an order delivered in the instant between the two passes **and** row-locked by
  something that issues no invoice (a review being submitted for it) is skipped and stays
  without an invoice. Not observed; a nightly "delivered, PAN on file, no invoice" sweep would
  close it and retry the refused ones.
- **On a dev database** the first PAN of a shop also invoices orders delivered before Phase 31.

### 2. Invoices: list and PDF (`/api/vendor/invoices`, `requireAuth(VENDOR)`, `no-store`)

```jsonc
// GET /api/vendor/invoices?fiscal_year=2082/083&document_type=INVOICE&limit=20&cursor=<invoice id>
{ "invoices": [ { "id", "document_type", "order_id", "fiscal_year", "bill_number",
                  "invoice_sequence": "HP-2082-000142", "issued_at", "issued_date_bs": "2082-06-22",
                  "buyer_name", "payment_method", "grand_total_npr", "print_count": 0 } ],
  "next_cursor": "uuid" | null }
// 400 INVALID_CURSOR (not this shop's invoice) · 400 VALIDATION_FAILED · 404 VENDOR_NOT_FOUND
// GET /api/vendor/invoices/:id/pdf → 200 application/pdf
//   Content-Disposition: inline; filename="HP-2082-000142.pdf" · X-Invoice-Copy-Number: 0
// 404 INVOICE_NOT_FOUND (also another shop's) · 400 VALIDATION_FAILED
```

- **List** (`VendorInvoiceService.list`): newest first, keyset on `(issued_at, id)` compared in
  SQL; limit 1–50, default 20. `print_count` = the invoice's PRINT rows. Not logged.
- **PDF** (`VendorInvoiceService.print`, `invoices/invoice-pdf.ts`), one transaction:
  1. the invoice row joined to the caller's shop, locked **`FOR UPDATE OF invoices`** (a lock,
     not a write: the row stays sealed). It is the only lock taken;
  2. `copy_number` = the count of its PRINT rows; insert the PRINT row (user, role, copy number,
     IP, user agent);
  3. render, **before the commit**: a print that cannot be rendered takes no number.
- Two simultaneous prints queue on the row lock and get consecutive numbers (tested with five);
  a partial unique index `(invoice_id, copy_number) WHERE action = 'PRINT'` backs it.
- **A GET with a side effect, on purpose:** every request is a print. It is `no-store`; a
  client that retries or prefetches makes a copy. The response is a buffer with
  `Content-Length`, not a chunked stream (an invoice is a few kB).
- **The document** (A4, pdfkit, built-in Helvetica): the copy mark (`ORIGINAL` /
  `COPY OF ORIGINAL (n)`), seller name, address, phone, `VAT No.` or `PAN`; `TAX INVOICE` for a
  VAT-registered seller, else `INVOICE`; buyer, payment method, order id; invoice number, Bill
  No., fiscal year, BS date, AD date and time in Nepal Time; the table (S.N., Particulars, HS
  Code, Qty, Rate, Discount, Taxable, VAT, Amount) with the header repeated on every page; the
  stored totals; the amount in words; on every page the disclaimer, the invoice number, the copy
  mark and "Page n of m".
  - **Nothing is computed:** every figure, date and the amount in words is the sealed row's.
    Amounts use the Nepali grouping (`1,02,500.50`).
  - **Deterministic:** the same row and copy number give the same bytes (`CreationDate` is the
    issue time).
- **`invoice_access_log`** (migration 0033): the columns of the table above; FKs to `invoices`
  and `users` (RESTRICT), each indexed; CHECK a copy number exactly for PRINT, never negative;
  hand-added triggers refuse UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE. Not in the Zod entity contract.
  - `TRUNCATE invoices` is now refused by PostgreSQL itself (the table is referenced);
    `TRUNCATE invoices CASCADE` by the triggers.

### 3. Vendor offers (`/api/vendor/offers`, `requireAuth(VENDOR)`, `no-store`)

```jsonc
// POST /api/vendor/offers { kind: "FLAT" | "PERCENTAGE", value, min_cart_npr? (0),
//                           max_discount_npr? (null), ends_at? (null) }   → 201 { offer }
//   400 VALIDATION_FAILED (a flat value above its minimum cart, a cap on a flat offer, > 100 %,
//       a vendor id / start date / status / label in the body)
//   422 OFFER_END_IN_PAST · 422 OFFER_LIMIT_REACHED (details.max 10) · 404 VENDOR_NOT_FOUND
// GET  /api/vendor/offers          → { offers: [ VendorOfferView ] }   newest first, at most 100
// POST /api/vendor/offers/:id/end  → 200 { offer }, also on repeat · 404 OFFER_NOT_FOUND (also another shop's)
// VendorOfferView: { id, kind, value, max_discount_npr, min_cart_npr, label, starts_at, ends_at,
//                    status: "ACTIVE" | "ENDED" | "CANCELLED", created_at, ended_at }
```

- **Table** (migration 0034, `schema/marketing.ts#vendorOffers`): §8Z.5's columns and CHECKs
  (value > 0, a percentage ≤ 100, a cap only on a percentage, a flat offer never above its
  minimum cart, `ends_at > starts_at`, ended at and by together). Indexes on every FK. Hand-added
  trigger `vendor_offers_guard`: INSERT only by the vendor's own user and never already ended;
  UPDATE only to end it, once, by the vendor's own user, with every other column unchanged;
  DELETE refused. Not in the Zod entity contract.
- **Service** (`marketing/vendor-offer-service.ts`): create and end each take the **vendor row
  `FOR UPDATE`**, then (end) the offer row; one transaction with the audit entry
  (`VENDOR_OFFER_CREATED` / `VENDOR_OFFER_ENDED`, both already in the contract). A repeated end
  answers the same row and records nothing.
- **`label`** is rendered by the server at creation (`vendorOfferLabel`: "Flat Rs. 100 OFF",
  "10% OFF", "20% OFF up to Rs. 100") and stored.
- **Limit (not asked):** at most 10 offers running or scheduled per shop, counted under the
  vendor lock, so checkout's later "best of the shop's offers" stays bounded.
- A flat offer always needs a minimum cart of at least its value, so `min_cart_npr` is optional
  only for a percentage.
- **No order is priced with an offer.** Checkout, the quote, settlement and the invoice ignore
  the table; `vendor_offer` in the quote is still null.

### Campaign discounts (SPEC core 7 and 9)

- **Which campaign.** `CheckoutService.runningCampaigns`: published, inside its dates on the
  database clock, and joined by the shop's own ACTIVE opt-in to its current terms. Without that
  row a campaign discounts nothing (SPEC verification 6, tested through the API).
- **How much** (`pricing.ts`, integer paisa): nothing below `min_cart_npr` (judged on the
  subtotal); FLAT its value; PERCENTAGE half-up to the paisa, capped at `max_discount_npr`;
  never more than the goods. Several campaigns: the larger discount, then the earlier opt-in.
- **Shares:** the vendor's share is rounded half-up once; the platform's is the remainder.
- **Commission** is charged on `subtotal - the vendor's share`. The minimum order value and the
  free-delivery threshold use the subtotal before the discount. The delivery fee is never reduced.
- **Quote:** `platform_promo: { id: <campaign id>, label: <campaign name>, discount_npr }`;
  `total_npr` is discounted. `vendor_offer` is still always null (no vendor offers exist).
- **Checkout** re-reads the opt-in `FOR SHARE` inside the order's transaction: closed since the
  cart was priced → `409 QUOTE_CHANGED`, no order, the inventory hold released. Lock order of a
  checkout: vendor row `FOR KEY SHARE`, opt-in row `FOR SHARE`, then the inserts.
- **One total.** `orderTotalPaisa(order)` (`@hamro-pasal/ledger`) = subtotal - discount +
  delivery fee. Used by the order views, the eSewa and Khalti amounts and their confirmation
  check, the mock payment, the refund-due event and the invoice. eSewa's `amount` field is the
  discounted goods, so `total_amount = amount + delivery charge` still holds.
- **Settlement** (`planSettlement`), with Dp the discount, Dpv the vendor's share, Dpp the
  platform's:

  | Order              | Postings                                                                                              |
  | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | prepaid            | escrow -(S-Dp+F), vendor +(S-Dpv-C) [+F own delivery], rider [+F], revenue +C, **PROMO_EXPENSE -Dpp** |
  | cash, own delivery | vendor +(Dpp-C), revenue +C, PROMO_EXPENSE -Dpp (the shop holds S-Dp+F in cash)                       |
  | cash, fleet        | rider -(S-Dp+F), vendor +(S-Dpv-C), revenue +C, rider +F, PROMO_EXPENSE -Dpp                          |

  `PROMO_EXPENSE` is one account opened on first use, like `PAYOUT_CLEARING`. Pending escrow and
  the vendor's "cut" figures subtract the vendor's share too.

- **Not built:** vendor offers and stacking; `payment_session` in the checkout response;
  `expected_total_npr`; the customer app showing the server's discount (it still shows its
  development-only mock "Shop Discount", §8Z.6, which now disagrees with a real campaign).

### The invoice (migration 0031)

- New columns, all NOT NULL: the seller copy (`seller_name` = legal name else business name,
  `seller_address` = registered address else the Palika, `seller_phone`, `seller_tax_id`,
  `seller_is_vat_registered`), `buyer_name` (first and last name, else "Customer"),
  `payment_method`, `taxable_amount_npr`, `vat_rate_percent`, `vat_amount_npr`,
  `exempt_amount_npr`, `delivery_charged_by`, `amount_in_words`, `line_items`.
- CHECKs: the PAN is nine digits; a seller that is not VAT registered shows no taxable amount and
  no VAT; **`grand_total = taxable + VAT + exempt (+ a platform delivery charge)`**.
- The migration requires an empty table (NOT NULL without defaults); nothing had issued one.
- **Arithmetic** (`computeInvoiceAmounts`, shared-types `localization/fiscal-invoice-math.ts`,
  moved unchanged from the Vendor App, which now imports it):
  - the discount is spread over the item lines by largest remainder, in whole paisa;
  - each taxed line is split on its own; **the header is the sum of the lines**, so it adds up to
    the total exactly (one split of the total can differ from the lines by a paisa or two);
  - the shop's own delivery charge is a taxed `DELIVERY` line; a fleet charge is in the total and
    outside taxable, VAT and exempt;
  - every discount lowers the taxable amount, the platform-funded share included.
- `generateFiscalInvoice` computes everything, **asserts the grand total equals
  `orderTotalPaisa(order)`** and the lines equal the order's subtotal, and only then takes the
  number. A mismatch throws: the delivery is not committed and no number is used.
- A seller with no PAN gets no invoice (`SELLER_HAS_NO_PAN`) and the delivery stands.

### Wiring

- `DeliveryHandoff.handOver`: settlement → ad premium → `generateFiscalInvoice`, one commit.
- `OrderReconciliationService`: for every order it reconciles (`ReconciledOrder.invoiceIssued`),
  after its own settlement and ad premium; an order the delivery invoiced is a replay.
- **Lock order of a delivery, and of a reconciliation:** order row → vendor row (`FOR NO KEY
UPDATE`) → ledger accounts → ad purchase row → ledger accounts → **invoice sequence row
  (`FOR UPDATE`), last**.

### Open

- **An order delivered while its shop had no PAN never gets an invoice.** Saving the PAN does not
  issue the waiting ones (SPEC core 10 says it should), and the reconciliation only sees an order
  once.
- No route reads an invoice (customer, vendor, admin), none prints one, and there are no Credit
  or Debit Notes. `hs_code` is always null and no product is VAT exempt (the columns do not
  exist); `buyer_tax_id`, `content_hash`, print and CBMS fields are not stored.
- A cancelled prepaid order's refund amount is the discounted total (what was paid); nothing pays
  refunds yet.
- The mock payment route and every other caller use the one total; the customer app's cart still
  computes its own pre-checkout total without the campaign.

### Automated payouts: views, finalize, fail

```jsonc
// every PayoutView (vendor ledger, settlement payout, admin list) gains, both defaulting to null:
"transfer_state": "PROCESSING_BANK_TRANSFER" | "COMPLETED" | "FAILED" | null,
"system_actor": "SETTLEMENT_PAYOUT_RUN" | null
// AdminPayoutView also: "primary_bank_account": { id, bank_name, branch_name, account_name,
//   account_number, routing_or_swift_code } | null   (sent only while PROCESSING_BANK_TRANSFER)
// GET  /api/admin/finance/payouts?status=&transfer_state=&limit=&cursor=
// POST /api/admin/finance/payouts/:id/finalize { bank_reference }  → 200 { payout }, also on repeat
// POST /api/admin/finance/payouts/:id/fail     { reason? }          → 200 { payout }, also on repeat
//   409 PAYOUT_NOT_PROCESSING (details.status, transfer_state) · 404 PAYOUT_NOT_FOUND · 400 VALIDATION_FAILED
```

- **finalize** (`AdminPayoutService.finalize`): `transfer_state = COMPLETED`, the bank reference,
  `decided_by_user_id` = the admin; `system_actor` stays. No money moves. Audit
  `PAYOUT_TRANSFER_COMPLETED`. The same reference again is 200; another one is 409.
- **fail**: the `VENDOR_PAYOUT_REVERSAL` journal a rejected request posts (PAYOUT_CLEARING →
  VENDOR_WALLET, key `vendor-payout-reversal:<payout>`), then `status = REJECTED`,
  `transfer_state = FAILED`, the reason, the admin. Through `LedgerService`, so it can lift a debt
  suspension (tested). Audit `PAYOUT_TRANSFER_FAILED`.
- Both act **only** on `PROCESSING_BANK_TRANSFER`: a manual settlement payout or a vendor's
  request is 409, and so is the legacy approve / reject on a run's payout (`PAYOUT_ALREADY_DECIDED`).
- **Locks:** the payout row `FOR UPDATE` first, then (fail only) the vendor row `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`
  and the ledger accounts inside `LedgerService.post`. The payout run and the admin's settlement
  payout only insert payout rows, so nothing takes these the other way round. A finalize racing a
  fail has one winner (tested, 6 rounds).
- **After a failure** the run's key `settlement-run:<date>` is still taken, so that run does not pay
  the shop again; the returned amount is in the next week's payout.
- Migration 0030: the transfer state CHECK (`TRANSFERRED` of 0028 became `COMPLETED`; nothing had
  written it), `system_actor` allowed on a REJECTED row, and the status CHECK: an APPROVED row
  either carries a bank reference and an admin, or is PROCESSING with a job and neither.
- **Admin app, `#/settlements`:** a "Bank transfers to make" section
  (`ProcessingTransfers.tsx`) under the shops table: vendor, primary bank account in full, amount,
  when the run prepared it, and **Mark Transferred** (asks the bank reference) / **Fail** (asks
  an optional reason, then "Return Rs. … to the wallet"). Mark Transferred is disabled while the
  shop has no primary account. Either answer refetches this list and the settlements list. It
  shows the first 50 and says when more are waiting.
- Not gated on the PAN again: the run paid under a verified PAN, and finalize records a transfer
  already made. A PAN changed in between does not block it.

### The ad premium in the nightly reconciliation

`OrderReconciliationService` (now constructed with the `LedgerService`) calls
`chargePerOrderAdPremium` right after a settlement **it posts itself**, in that order's
transaction; an order the delivery settled is not charged again. `ReconciledOrder.adPremiumNpr`
reports it. Locks as in a delivery: order row → vendor row (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`) → accounts → ad
purchase row → accounts. A mismatch or a failed settlement rolls the charge back with it.

### Fiscal invoicing: schema and `generateFiscalInvoice` (not wired)

- **Migration 0029:** enum `fiscal_document_type`; `invoice_sequences`; `invoices` (`id`,
  `document_type`, `vendor_id`, `order_id`, `customer_id`, `fiscal_year`, `bill_number`,
  `invoice_sequence`, `issued_at`, `issued_date_bs`, `subtotal_npr`, `discount_npr`,
  `delivery_charge_npr`, `grand_total_npr`). Unique `(vendor_id, document_type, fiscal_year,
bill_number)`; one INVOICE per order (partial unique index); CHECK `grand_total = subtotal −
discount + delivery`. Neither table is in the Zod entity contract.
- **Hand-added triggers:** `invoices` refuses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE outright;
  `invoice_sequences` starts at 0, changes only by `last_number + 1`, and is never deleted or
  truncated.
- **`generateFiscalInvoice(tx, order, issuedAt?)`** (`packages/ledger/src/fiscal-invoice.ts`, so
  the API's delivery and the worker can both call it; `fiscalYearOf` joined `bs-calendar.ts`):
  1. the order must be DELIVERED (`InvoiceNotIssuableError`, before the counter is touched);
  2. the issue time is the database clock; its Nepal Time date gives the fiscal year;
  3. `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` opens the seller's counter, then
     **`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`** on that row;
  4. under the lock: the order already has its invoice → that invoice, `replayed: true`, no number;
  5. `UPDATE … last_number + 1 RETURNING`, then the invoice row.
- **Lock order:** the caller holds the order row; the sequence row is taken last and nothing is
  locked after it. When it is wired into `DeliveryHandoff` it must come after the settlement and
  the ad premium.
- A rollback returns the number; 20 simultaneous deliveries of one shop get 1 to 20.

**What the invoice is not yet (must be added before it is wired).** It is a header with totals.
SPEC core 10 also requires, on the same sealed row: the seller's name, address and **PAN** as
issued, the VAT split (13%) and exempt amount, the itemised lines with HS codes, the payment
method, the buyer's name, the amount in words, and the print / CBMS fields. None is stored, so
**this row alone is not an IRD invoice**. `discount_npr` is always 0 (orders carry no discount).
Because the table refuses UPDATE, those columns have to land (as NOT NULL) before the first real
invoice, not after.

### Open

- Wiring: `DeliveryHandoff.handOver` (and the reconciliation's own settlement) do not issue an
  invoice; no read, print or note route; no Vendor App or customer screen reads one.
- The legacy Payouts tab does not show `transfer_state`; a run's payout appears there as APPROVED.
- "Bank transfers to make" has no paging beyond 50, and no component test.
- `GET /api/admin/finance/settlements` still has no `next_run_at` / `cutoff_at`.

### Tests

- **API integration 782 in 48 suites; 781 passed in the one full run.** The failure,

## 8Z.30 Phase 29: payment routing by settlement model, the model locked on orders, the ad premium at delivery, the weekly payout run (2026-10-08)

Backend only (`packages/shared-types`, `packages/db`, `packages/ledger`, `apps/api`, `apps/worker`).
Migration **0028**. SPEC.md was not changed. **Not run against a live API or worker**; the dev
database needs `pnpm db:migrate`.

### Asked vs built

| Asked                                                     | Built                                                                                                                                                                          | Why                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0028_order_settlement_lock.sql` for the orders column    | the same file also changes `payout_requests` (two columns, the status CHECK)                                                                                                   | One `drizzle-kit generate`; the payout run could not store its rows otherwise                                                              |
| an APPROVED payout row, "state: PROCESSING_BANK_TRANSFER" | `status = APPROVED`, new column `transfer_state = PROCESSING_BANK_TRANSFER`, new column `system_actor = SETTLEMENT_PAYOUT_RUN`, `bank_reference` and `decided_by_user_id` null | The old CHECK required an admin and a bank reference on every APPROVED row. `payout_status` keeps its three values, so no API view changed |
| pay shops with "an available balance >= 1000"             | what was in the wallet **at the cut-off** (Monday 00:00 NPT), less every debit since, capped by what is available now; paid when that is at least 1000                         | SPEC core 5 and verification 22 (decided 2026-10-07)                                                                                       |
| `chargePerOrderAdPremium(tx, order_id, vendor_id)`        | `chargePerOrderAdPremium(tx, ledger, orderId, vendorId)`, called by `DeliveryHandoff.handOver`                                                                                 | The function as Phase 28 built it                                                                                                          |
| Model C                                                   | offered no payment method at all (`reason: SETTLEMENT_MODEL`)                                                                                                                  | Not selectable and not built; a shop can only be on it by SQL                                                                              |

### Payment routing (SPEC core 9)

- `SETTLEMENT_MODEL_PAYMENT_METHODS` (shared-types `domain/enums.ts`): `COD_CREDIT` → COD;
  `PLATFORM_ESCROW` → eSewa, Khalti, COD; `DIRECT_PREPAID` → none.
- `offeredPaymentMethods(shop)` (`checkout-service.ts`) = that list ∩ `vendors.accepted_payment_methods`.
  The shop's own list only narrows: a Model A shop that accepts no cash can take no order.
- **Quote:** `payment_options[].reason` gained `SETTLEMENT_MODEL`. Precedence: `DELIVERY_UNAVAILABLE`,
  `SETTLEMENT_MODEL`, `NOT_ACCEPTED_BY_SHOP`, `COD_NOT_AVAILABLE`.
- **Checkout:** `422 PAYMENT_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE`, `details { accepted, reason, settlement_model }`
  (`reason`: `SETTLEMENT_MODEL` or `NOT_ACCEPTED_BY_SHOP`). Checked before the COD rating check and
  the inventory lock, and **again inside the order's transaction** (below).
- `cartQuoteResponseSchema` is strict: an app build must know the new reason before it calls the
  quote (the customer app does not call it yet).

### `orders.settlement_model_locked` (migration 0028)

- `settlement_model NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PLATFORM_ESCROW'`; in `orderSchema` and `contract.ts`.
  Existing orders were backfilled from their shop's current model (no earlier record exists).
- Hand-added trigger `orders_settlement_model_locked_immutable`: any UPDATE that changes the
  column is refused (SQLSTATE 23000).
- **Written under a lock.** Inside the order's transaction checkout reads
  `vendors.settlement_model` and `accepted_payment_methods` `FOR KEY SHARE`, re-checks the payment
  method against them, and copies the model. A settlement model approval takes the vendor row
  `FOR UPDATE`: it either committed first (the order takes the new model, or is refused by it and
  its Redis hold released), or it waits and then counts the order as open.
- **Nothing reads the column yet.** Settlement is the same for A and B today (`planSettlement`
  reads the payment method and fulfilment); the column is for the first rule that differs.

### The ad premium at delivery

- `DeliveryHandoff.handOver` calls `chargePerOrderAdPremium` after `settleOrderInTransaction`, in
  the delivery's transaction, for the rider's and the vendor's handoff alike. The container passes
  the one `LedgerService`.
- **A Model B fee may take the wallet negative on a cash order (decided 2026-10-08).** It goes
  through `WalletService` like the commission, so crossing the limit suspends the shop in the same
  commit and the delivery stands (tested at -2015).
- A charge that uses up the budget pauses the ad and audits `AD_PAUSED_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`
  (`system_actor` `AD_ORDER_PREMIUM`) in that commit; later orders are delivered uncharged.
- **Lock order of a delivery:** order row (`FOR UPDATE`) → vendor row (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`,
  the settlement journal) → ledger accounts by id → vendor row again (already held) → ad purchase
  row (`FOR UPDATE`) → ledger accounts by id.
- **Deadlock found and fixed.** `chargePerOrderAdPremium` locked the vendor row `FOR UPDATE`. After
  a settlement journal that is a lock upgrade, and two deliveries of one shop deadlocked (the second
  already queued behind the first's weaker lock). It now takes `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, which still
  excludes every other ad path (they take `FOR UPDATE`). **Rule: after a wallet journal, never ask
  for a stronger lock on that vendor row; a path that needs `FOR UPDATE` takes it first.**
- Not done: the nightly reconciliation does not charge a premium for a settlement it posts itself;
  `orders.ad_order_premium` does not exist (the fee is on the ledger and the purchase).

### `SETTLEMENT_PAYOUT_RUN` (`apps/worker/src/finance/settlement-payout-run.ts`)

- Scheduler `settlement-payout-run` on the maintenance queue: cron `0 2 * * 2`, `Asia/Kathmandu`,
  3 attempts (`SETTLEMENT_PAYOUT_RUN_TASK`, `SETTLEMENT_PAYOUT_CRON_PATTERN`,
  `SETTLEMENT_PAYOUT_MIN_NPR` in shared-types `jobs/queues.ts`).
- `payoutCutoff(now)`: the first instant of the Monday of the run's week in Nepal Time.
- Candidates (unlocked): Model B, `pan_verified_at` set, wallet at least 1000. Then **one
  transaction per vendor**:
  1. vendor row `FOR UPDATE`; model and PAN re-read (`NOT_ELIGIBLE`);
  2. a payout row with key `settlement-run:<cut-off date>` exists → `ALREADY_PAID`;
  3. no primary bank account → `NO_PRIMARY_BANK_ACCOUNT`;
  4. `collectAdFeesDue` (flat fees owed leave the wallet first, and stay collected);
  5. amount = min(max(0, wallet postings before the cut-off + debits since), available now);
     under 1000 → `BELOW_MINIMUM`;
  6. the Phase 22 `VENDOR_PAYOUT` journal (key `settlement-run:<date>:<vendor>`), the payout row,
     and `PAYOUT_PROCESSED` audited with `{ kind: 'SYSTEM', job: 'SETTLEMENT_PAYOUT_RUN' }` (masked
     account number, `cutoff_at`, `transfer_state`).
- Locks: vendor row → ad purchase rows → ledger accounts, the admin payout's order.
- A vendor that fails does not stop the others; the job then fails and BullMQ retries it, which
  pays nobody twice.
- `ad-fees.ts` moved to `@hamro-pasal/ledger` (the API keeps a re-export) so the worker collects
  fees with the API's code. The run is its own service, not `AdminSettlementService` (that class
  lives in the API): the journal, gates and fee collection are the same, the code is not shared.

### Open

- **No route moves a payout out of `PROCESSING_BANK_TRANSFER`.** An admin has nowhere to record
  the bank reference of a run's payout, or to reverse one whose transfer failed. `TRANSFERRED` is
  allowed by the CHECK and written by nothing.
- The vendor's and the admin's payout views do not carry `transfer_state`: a run's payout shows
  as APPROVED with no bank reference.
- `GET /api/admin/finance/settlements` has no `next_run_at` / `cutoff_at`.
- The run pays suspended shops too (as a manual payout may).
- Model A's credit rule, recharge, and the Model A branch of settlement are still unbuilt.

### Tests

- **API integration 757 in 46 suites, all passing** (one full run). New
  `settlement-rules-and-ad-charging.int.test.ts` (14): routing per model and its intersection, the
  422 with nothing created and no stock held, Model C; the locked model at creation, after a model
  change, refused by the database, and **a checkout racing a model change**; the premium in a cash
  and a prepaid delivery, a retried delivery, a wrong code, an order placed before the ad, the

- **Worker:** new `settlement-payout-run.int.test.ts` (13, real PostgreSQL): the cut-off instants;
  the paid row, journal and audit entry; money credited after the cut-off waiting a week; debits
  since; 1000 vs 999.99; unverified, no bank account, Model A; four concurrent runs and a rerun;
  ad fees first; **a run racing a PAN change**; the CHECKs; the task dispatch.
  `queues.int.test` asserts the Tuesday scheduler (Monday 20:15 UTC). **The full worker
  suite in one command did not finish (stopped after 10 minutes, no output).** Run suite by suite,
  all 12 pass (98 tests) except that `vendor-notifications.int` "dead-letters a poison pill at
  once" timed out in 2 of 5 runs and passed in the others, also with these changes stashed: the
  Kafka flake §1 records. No Kafka or notification code changed.
- db integration 140, unit suites unchanged in count and passing (mobile 1505, shared-types 295,
  admin 285, worker 142, api 114, ledger 16). `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint`: 16 of 16.
- **Mutation-checked, 10 of 10 killed:** routing ignoring the model (4 fail), model not written
  (2), no re-check under the vendor lock (1), no premium at delivery (5); no cut-off (3), debits
  ignored (1), no minimum (1), no vendor row lock (1), no PAN re-read (1), fees not collected (1).
  The last two vendor-lock mutants survived until the PAN race test was added. The `FOR UPDATE` in

### `GET /api/home/promotions` (public, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`)

```jsonc
{ "banners": [ { "id", "placement": "CAROUSEL", "image_url", "title", "subtitle",
                 "target_type": "SHOP" | "CATEGORY" | "DISCOUNT_TAG" | null, "target_value", "is_sponsored" } ],

```

  `ends_at` null or future (database clock), by `display_order`, then creation.

  under a hidden parent), **or it is sponsored and its ad purchase is no longer running**

  (`api/admin-marketing.ts`). Route `routes/home.ts`, mounted at `/api/home`.

### `chargePerOrderAdPremium(tx, ledger, orderId, vendorId)` (`packages/ledger/src/ad-order-premium.ts`)

**Built and tested; not called by any delivery yet.** To wire it: call it in
`DeliveryHandoff.handOver` after `settleOrderInTransaction`, in the same transaction.

| Outcome              | When                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `NONE`               | no ACTIVE per-order purchase of the shop covers the order's `placed_at`; unknown order or another shop's                                                                                                     |
| `CHARGED` (`paused`) | one fee posted (`AD_PURCHASE` journal `ad-order-premium:<purchase>:<order>`, both lines `AD_ORDER_PREMIUM`), `amount_paid_npr` raised. `paused`: less than one fee is left, the ad is now PAUSED and audited |
| `ALREADY_CHARGED`    | that order was charged before: nothing posted                                                                                                                                                                |
| `PAUSED_UNCHARGED`   | the budget did not hold one fee: the ad is paused and the order is **not** charged (SPEC edge case 8)                                                                                                        |

- Locks: vendor row (`FOR UPDATE`), purchase row, then the ledger accounts.
- The pause is audited with `system_actor` `AD_ORDER_PREMIUM`.
- **To decide before wiring:** a Model B shop's fee comes out of its wallet. After a prepaid
  order's settlement the wallet covers it; after a **cash** order it can take the wallet negative
  (as the commission does) and so count toward the debt suspension limit.
- The nightly reconciliation compares only the settlement journal, so this separate journal does
  not disturb it.

### Vendor App and search

- "Your ads": each purchase shows `Ad ID: <first 8 characters>` with "Tap to copy"; the tap
  shares the whole uuid (`shortAdId`, `ad-id-<id>`).
- Home search: the feed's sponsored entries lead the shop results of every search, whether or not
  their name matches, each with the card's "Ad" badge; a sponsored shop that also matches is
  listed once. Product results are unchanged.

### Tests

Run on 2026-10-08 in a fresh session (the session that wrote the code ended before it could record a run).

- **API integration** 743 in 45 suites, **all passing** in one full run. New `ad-premium-and-home-promotions.int.test.ts` (8, real PostgreSQL): one fee per order as its own `AD_ORDER_PREMIUM` lines, a retried order charged once, the ad paused with one audit entry when the budget runs out and no order charged after; a Model A shop's fee drawn from `AD_BUDGET_CLEARING` with its wallet untouched and a later cancel returning only the undrawn part; nothing for an order placed before the ad, another shop's order or an unknown order; six simultaneous deliveries on a budget of two fees → two charges, one pause; pause without a charge when the budget holds less than one fee. Home promotions: public, `max-age=60`, active and inside its dates, grouped and ordered; a shop that stops being LIVE or a hidden category drops its promotion and brings it back; a sponsored banner flagged, then dropped when the vendor cancels the purchase.
- **A flake found and fixed in that file's fixture.** An earlier full run failed the sponsored-banner test once. Cause: the fixture bought an ad with `starts_at` = this process's "now", and "running" is decided on the database clock, which was measured 22 ms behind the host (Docker Desktop). The fixture ad now starts a minute earlier. `vendor-ads-api.int.test.ts` builds its purchases the same way (`starts_at: new Date()`) and has not failed, but can for the same reason.
- **Mutation-checked, 3 of 3 killed:** no "budget holds one fee" check before charging (1 test fails), a non-LIVE shop's promotion served (1), a sponsored promotion served without a running purchase (1).
- Unit suites, all passing: mobile **1505** in 102 suites (+7; new `features/promo/live-promotions.test.tsx`), shared-types 295, ledger 16, api 114, worker 142, admin 285. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint`: all 16 tasks pass.

## 8Z.28 Phase 28, part 2: Vendor App Marketing wired, the hourly ad status sweep, the sponsored feed (2026-10-08)

Mobile (`apps/mobile`), worker, API and two shared contracts. **No migration.** SPEC.md was not
changed. **Not seen on a device and not run against a live API or worker.**

### Decision (user, 2026-10-08)

A flat-rate ad cannot be cancelled once it has started (it runs to its end at the price agreed); a
per-order ad can be cancelled at any time, releasing the unused budget. §8Z.27's "to confirm" is
closed; the code was already so.

### Asked vs built

| Asked                                                     | Built                                                                                                | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the sweep marks ended **campaigns** `COMPLETED` / `ENDED` | **nothing is written for campaigns**                                                                 | `platform_campaigns` has no status column: "ended" is derived from `ends_at` on the database clock everywhere it matters (the opt-in refuses with `422 CAMPAIGN_ENDED`, the vendor list leaves ended campaigns out). `is_active` means "published", and flipping it would be an admin's unpublish done by a job. A stored status needs a migration and a contract change in the admin app: say if you want it |
| end ACTIVE purchases past `ends_at`                       | ACTIVE **and PAUSED** ones, and the unused part of a held budget is released in the same transaction | A paused ad's period ends too, and a Model A budget would otherwise stay held for ever                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| pause when `amount_paid_npr >= budget_npr`                | pause when `budget − paid < price`                                                                   | SPEC edge case 8: an ad whose budget cannot cover the **next** fee is paused before that order is charged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| a new BullMQ job, hourly                                  | an hourly scheduler (`0 * * * *`) on the existing maintenance queue, id `marketing-status-sweep`     | One queue and one worker already run the crons; the job schema and processor dispatch the new task apart from the midnight tasks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| starts_at input                                           | four choices: Now, in 1, 3 or 7 days                                                                 | No date picker is installed (a native dependency and a dev-client rebuild); the server takes any instant up to 90 days ahead                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### The hourly sweep (`apps/worker/src/marketing/marketing-status-sweep.ts`)

- Task `MARKETING_STATUS_SWEEP` (shared-types `jobs/queues.ts`: `MARKETING_STATUS_SWEEP_TASK`,
  `HOURLY_CRON_PATTERN`), registered by `registerMidnightJobs`, handled by
  `TimerHandlers.runMarketingStatusSweep`. 3 attempts.
- **Ends** every ACTIVE or PAUSED purchase with `ends_at <= now()`: `ENDED`, audit `AD_ENDED`
  (new action; `system_actor` = the job; `after_state.returned_npr`). A held per-order budget
  (Models A / C) goes back through `releaseUnusedAdBudget` (new, in `@hamro-pasal/ledger`; the
  vendor's cancel uses the same function and the same journal key, so the two can never both
  release). A flat fee a Model B shop still owes **stays due** after the ad ends.
- **Pauses** ACTIVE per-order ads with less than one fee of budget left: `PAUSED`, audit
  `AD_PAUSED_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. Nothing posts a per-order premium yet, so this finds nothing
  today.
- One transaction per purchase; locks vendor row, then purchase row, then ledger accounts; the
  condition is re-read under the locks on the database clock. A rerun or four concurrent runs
  change a purchase once (tested).
- This unblocks the settlement model change of a shop whose ads are over (§8Z.27 "Open"), within
  the hour.

### Sponsored feed (`GET /api/vendors`)

- `feedEntrySchema.is_sponsored` (boolean, **defaults to false**, so an app build reads an older
  API as "no ads").
- `CatalogService.listFeed`: shops with a FEED_LISTING purchase that is ACTIVE and inside its
  period are the advertisers. `withSponsoredFirst` moves the **nearest two** that are serviceable
  and whose delivery mode is on to the top of `serviceable`, flagged; everyone else, a third
  advertiser included, keeps its place unflagged. `explore_further` is never touched. Applied
  before the 100-per-section cap.
- A shop already had to be LIVE to be in the feed. A purchase that starts later, was cancelled or
  has ended (by clock, even before the sweep marks it) does not count.
- Mobile: `VendorCard` shows the "Ad" badge for `entry.is_sponsored` (the development mock flag
  still draws it too); `sortFeed` keeps flagged entries first under every sort.
- Not done: the Home search results (`GET /api/products`) carry no sponsorship; "Sponsored
  Search" is the feed listing only.

  → the same toast, sheet closed; `AD_BUDGET_INVALID` → the budget field.

AD_PURCHASE_NOT_CANCELLABLE` (a phone clock that is behind) shows the same warning as a toast.

### Migration 0027 (`0027_ledger_lines_ads.sql`)

  `AD_BUDGET_HOLD` or `AD_BUDGET_RELEASE` line names a purchase. With the Phase 27 trigger on

  already used (`ensureSingletonAccount`). No unique index enforces either singleton.
- **Nothing is backfilled.** Every existing posting, and every non-ad posting written from now on,
